newsitem.title: BOSNIA: U.S. defence secretary visits Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. defence secretary visits Bosnia.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry arrived in Bosnia on Thursday to visit American troops and hold talks with NATO officers about a new peace force bound for Bosnia next year.
Perry was greeted by U.S. army General George Joulwan, commander of NATO forces in Europe, and other senior U.S. officers at the start of a five-hour visit.
Later on this second day of a globe-circling trip, Perry was due to fly on to Kuwait.
Perry was due to eat a traditional Thanksgiving lunch of turkey with American, Russian and other troops at a nearby camp and later meet Russian officers.
U.S. and Russian troops will form part of the new 31,000-strong peacekeeping force in Bosnia.
The new "stabilisation force" will replace a current 50,000 NATO-led peace implementation force (IFOR) now being withdrawan after a year in Bosnia.
The new "SFOR" would remain in the country until mid-1998 to provide security and stability as the international community attempts to mend Bosnia's ruined economy.

A U.S.-brokered peace treaty agreed in November last year ended fighting in Bosnia but diplomats say war could resume between Bosnia's Moslems, Serbs and Croats without the continued presence of the NATO-led force.
Perry told reporters on Wednesday in Naples at the start of the trip that SFOR could not guarantee peace and stability in the former Yugoslav republic.
"Fundamentally, the Bosnians themselves are going to have to make those changes," he said. "I think the key to whether they will want to do that is success in the economic restructuring."
Perry told reporters travelling with him that he was not worried about the security of next year's new reduced Bosnia force, which will include 8,500 U.S. troops.
Some 15,000 American troops serve in the current force.

"I want to emphasize the most important point I can make on this is that these were not numbers that were conceived in Washington and handed to the field with a 'see if you can make this work'," Perry said.
